Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testExistingFilePattern` fails because the option type `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` which corresponds to `FileInputStream.class` is not properly checked for file existence, leading to the returned object not being of type `FileInputStream`. The `PatternOptionBuilder.parsePattern` creates options with types derived from a pattern, and the `<` character maps to `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` which is `FileInputStream.class`.

In `CommandLine.getParsedOptionValue`, the option value (a string) is converted to the expected type through `TypeHandler.createValue`. When the type is `EXISTING_FILE_VALUE` (`FileInputStream.class`), the code currently calls `createFile(str)`, which returns a `File` object, not a `FileInputStream`, ignoring the expectation of the file's existing status and the correct object type.

This causes the test to fail at the assertion that expects the parsed option value to be a `FileInputStream`. The core issue is that `createValue` does not distinguish or instantiate a `FileInputStream` but returns a plain `File` object, ignoring the file existence or wrapping in a `FileInputStream`. 

The bug report also confirms this, pointing out that when specifying option type `FileInputStream.class`, users expect to receive that type, presumably after verifying the file exists. The current code fails to fulfill that contract. This diagnosis aligns with the observed failure in the test and the discrepancy in the type of the returned parsed option value.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
